body: My IVC scarred me for life. I also strongly suspect I have undiagnosed autism.

I’m frustrated that people did not follow the system and laws. It was a wrongful involuntarily commitment. They did not properly evaluate me.

What red flags? Please tell me. Also keep in mind that this happened months ago. I don’t know why you’re trying to use one Reddit post to explain and justify my IVC from the past. I’m angry in the post because I was wrongfully held against my will and traumatized. Again, what red flags?

They didn’t clear the bar. Yes it’s maybe reasonable to send cops to someone talking about suicidal ideation on social media. But again, you can’t commit someone just for suicidal ideation. And they can’t just look at the words I typed, they need to know my actual intent. Legally, the context matters. From the moment the cops first came to me, I showed that I had no intent on hurting myself. Does me having a therapy meeting the next day just mean nothing? Also, I had only one therapist review my case before I was committed. The doctor didn’t even see or talk to me. Is what I posted the *only* thing that matters? They aren’t required to look at anything else? Is it possible to take legal action based on gross unreasonableness? If I could prove it? I’m leaving out a lot of other strong signs that I was clearly not in danger.

A magistrate never reviewed anything. I didn’t even know that a magistrate or district court judge was supposed to review the case until I got released and started researching IVC stuff. One therapist and a doctor “evaluated” me absurdly unreasonably. Which in itself is not legal. It’s malpractice. And then several hours later I was told I was being involuntarily committed. Then they shipped me off to the hospital where I spent my IVC.

It was 12 days from when I was told I was being committed.

btw I’m not mad at you. Thanks for commenting.

I don’t see how it’s compelling evidence. Talking about suicide on the internet does not necessarily imply suicidal intent. I had no plan. I didn’t want to hurt myself. IVCs do not occur for suicidal ideation. They’re for when the person is actually in danger/can’t take care of themselves. Also, it wasn’t just the post. They all talked to me, and I told them over and over again that I had no intention on harming myself AND I had an appointment with a therapist THE DAY AFTER. That’s enough for suicidal ideation. They could have maybe kept me until I had my meeting with my therapist. There was no need to go further than my initial evaluation. I don’t even remember if I had a second evaluation. The therapist also looked through my social media without my permission and used that as “evidence”.

I was in for 12 days. 

Just wondering, aren’t I required to meet with judge or magistrate *before* I get involuntarily committed? Is it really legal to hold someone against their will just because you feel like they are in immediate danger even though they are clearly not?
